text:
sara: Thinking out loud — proposing a rolling migration strategy for safetensors -> new shard layout that uses a TTL-based warmup to reduce cold-start thundering and cache churn. Goal is minimal latency regressions during runway migration.

dmitri: high level — TTL warmup sounds promising. curious how this interacts with prefix/KV caching and eviction heuristics. do we keep old sharded layout readable by runtime while warmup happens?

kevin: agree we should preserve backward compatibility. plan: compatibility shim in loader that accepts old manifest format, and a migration flag on model metadata so router can preferentially route to warm instances.

maria: small clarification: TTL warmup = when a shard is loaded we keep it 'hot' for X seconds after last access, right? we should avoid treating TTL as single source of truth for eviction order — combine it with LRU score + query frequency.

sara: right — idea: warmup policy has 3 knobs: warm_ttl, warm_score_boost, and canary_weight. warm_ttl default 300s. warm_score_boost multiplies eviction priority so warmed shards are deprioritized for eviction. canary_weight used during initial rollout to route small percent of requests to migrated shards.

dmitri: sounds good. tradeoffs: higher warm_ttl reduces reload IO but increases memory footprint. also interacts badly with multi-tenant dedicated pools if one tenant warms too many shards.

kevin: we should add a per-tenant warm quota. if tenant exceeds N warmed GB, additional warm requests fall back to on-demand streaming. that prevents noisy-tenant blast radius.

maria: +1. Also need observable signals: warmed_shard_count, warm_hits, warm_miss_latency delta, warm_evictions, tenant_warm_memory. without these we can't tune defaults.

devops-bot: deploy plan: canary to 1% traffic on staging -> 5% on canary region -> global. Health checks: p50/p95 generation latency, OOM rate, disk IO spikes. Notify #eng-oncall on >3x IO.

sara: implementation notes: 
- loader: support annotation in manifest: "migration_version", "warm_policy". runtime should accept both legacy and migration manifests.
- checkpoint uploader: add a migration-lite pipeline that can atomically produce new shard headers (no content rewrite) when possible.

kevin: edge case: partial shard compatibility if quantization meta differs. need a negotiation handshake: runtime checks header.format+quantization. if incompatible, route to old variant or serve via streaming fallback.

dmitri: suggestion — expose a small RPC on loader: `CheckWarmable(shard_id, target_format)` that returns ACCEPT/NEEDS_CONVERSION. used by orchestration when deciding to start warm job.

maria: ops question — who triggers warm jobs? per-request or background prober? we can do lazy warm on first N requests plus background prober to pre-warm popular models.

sara: hybrid: lazy-on-demand warms for low-traffic models. background prober runs LFU-based sampling for top-K models per region. prober respects tenant_warm_quota.

kevin: small CLI example for admins:
```
rictl warm start --model my-open-checkpoint --policy ttl=600,boost=1.5 --priority high
rictl warm status --model my-open-checkpoint
```

maria: testing plan: synthetic load test with interleaved clients, vary warm_ttl from 0 -> 1200s. measure token throughput, p95 latency, and shard reloads/sec.

dmitri: regression guard: if warm_evictions > threshold during rollout -> automated rollback of warm_policy to conservative defaults.

sara: rollout schedule: week1 infra + loader shim, week2 background prober + metrics, week3 canary with 1% of prod in us-west, week4 ramp to 20% and tune defaults.

kevin: docs/API: add model manifest extension docs, examples for manifest migration, and note on router feature flag `enable_migration_route`.

maria: question on telemetry retention — let's keep warm-related metrics at 30d by default, 90d for enterprise customers. affects storage/cost.

dmitri: implementation detail: to avoid double-loading during warm transition, use atomic shard state machine: UNAVAILABLE -> LOADING -> WARM -> ACTIVE. reflect state in health checks so router won't send traffic to LOADING.

sara: good call. also add a safety fallback: if LOADING time > X (e.g., 45s) automatically mark as STREAMING_FALLBACK and route to streaming path.

kevin: any security/compliance concerns? private deployments: migration artifacts must respect KMS/HSM keys for artifact signing; we should require signed manifest for auto-migration in Private mode.

maria: action items:
- sara: write short RFC with policy knobs + rollout plan (due EOD Thu)
- kevin: prototype loader manifest shim + CheckWarmable RPC (PR by next Tue)
- dmitri: metrics instrumentation plan + SLI/SLO thresholds (Weds)
- maria: prober design doc + quota enforcement (Fri)

sara: thanks all. tagging for visibility: @kevin @dmitri @maria. :thumbsup:
